entries.officialText:
A skew-symmetric determinant of even order is
(A) zero
(B) perfect square
(C) not a perfect square
(D) Non zero
entries.reasoning: A skew-symmetric matrix of even order n has det A = det(A^T) = det(-A) = (-1)^n det A, which for even n constrains nothing by itself; the stronger classical result is that the determinant of an even-order skew-symmetric matrix is the square of its Pfaffian, hence a perfect square. Counter-direction check: it is the *odd*-order case that is forced to zero, which is why option A is the trap.
entries.verification: Exact integer arithmetic over 100 sampled skew-symmetric matrices of order 2 and 4: every determinant is k*k for an integer k.

machineCheck.method: exact integer determinant test over 100 sampled skew-symmetric matrices
machineCheck.expected: det = k*k for an integer k, for every even-order skew-symmetric matrix

A thin cylinder with 180 cm internal diameter and 12 mm thickness is subjected to internal pressure of 1.2 MPa. The maximum shear stress developed at any point in the internal wall is
(A) 42.6 MPa
(B) 43.6 MPa
(C) 44.6 MPa
(D) 45.6 MPa
entries.reasoning: sigma_h = pd/2t = 90 MPa and sigma_l = pd/4t = 45 MPa; at the inner wall the radial stress is -p = -1.2 MPa, so the maximum shear is (90 + 1.2)/2 = 45.6 MPa.
entries.verification: tau = 45.60 MPa with the radial stress included.
